title: Dress for Weather ABC
hook: Wear what helps now; change it when the weather changes.
roundStructure: Round 1 lexical-semantic A-Z; Round 2 retrieval-action A-Z; 4+4+4+4+4+4+2 chunks
visualStyle: cheerful 3D weather-gear storybook, colorful coats boots and sky cues, clean child-safe objects, simple background

creativeFingerprint.pointOfView: a child making simple weather clothing decisions with adult guidance
creativeFingerprint.round1Grammar: hand-written condition-response pairs; gear, instruments, hazards and sky terms remain distinct
creativeFingerprint.round2Grammar: condition cue -> recall beat -> target -> safe gear/point gesture
creativeFingerprint.sectionContrast: Verses stay sparse; chorus widens; retrieval strips back. glockenspiel or marimba weather-signals after the word, with percussion ducking on onset
creativeFingerprint.signatureColor: glockenspiel or marimba weather-signals after the word, with percussion ducking on onset
creativeFingerprint.authorialIntent: Make Dress for Weather a decision song: first identify the condition, then choose a sensible layer or protection; instruments explain why, and non-gear targets never get forced into clothing language.
creativeFingerprint.lyricIdentity: A child asks condition first, clothing second—cold, wet, windy, warm—while radar and meters stay in the information column.
semanticArc: finish by adjusting layers rather than dressing for one permanent forecast
